nodes.question: What does the analysis identify about the methodology of HIA?
nodes.answer: The analysis identifies different paradigms operating in the field of HIA and varying perspectives on how HIA methodology is theorized and practiced.
nodes.paragraph: It is recognised as a benefi - cial tool to drive consideration of Health in All Policies [10 12]. HIA has been embraced globally by the World Health Organisation (WHO), some governments and nation states but most research and practice has taken place in Europe, North America and Oceania [ 1, 12, 13]. A recent bibliographic analysis of published journal papers and research activities for HIAs since 2015 depicts a field of diverse interests and perspectives which have emerged as HIA has evolved [ 14]. They range from inves - tigating health in EIA, transport and active travel HIAs, quantitative modelling, evaluation and effectiveness and social determinant and equity driven HIA case studies. The paper also identifies different paradigms which are operating in the field of HIA and as part of considering health in Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). The analysis identified different perspectives on how HIA methodology is theorised and practiced. One world view to knowledge generation and evidence focuses on what is observable and measurable, leading to HIAs based on quantifiable impacts including environmental health determinants such as air quality, noise, emissions and these being the primary sources of evidence to create an understanding of the health impact of a proposal.

nodes.question: According to Payne et al. (2021), what is the approach taken to reviewing policies in Australia?
nodes.answer: Payne et al. (2021) adopt an approach to reviewing policies in Australia that involves analysing their effectiveness, sustainability, feasibility, and compliance.

nodes.question: What does the "Analysis and Findings" section present in the study?
nodes.answer: The "Analysis and Findings" section presents the analysis and key findings of the study.
nodes.paragraph: This study employs a mixed-methods approach incorporating word analysis, sentiment analysis, topic modelling, and exploratory qualitative analysis to com- prehensively understand user experiences, perceptions, and engagement with the app. It analyses public user reviews and identifies recurring themes such as user motivations, perceived app value, and reported chal- lenges. These findings contribute to the broader dis- course on the digitalization of energy services, uncover - ing general trends in user engagement and identifying opportunities to enhance app design and functionality to promote energy-conscious practices. Overall, this study is guided by the following research question: RQ How do user interactions with energy appli- cations shape engagement, perceptions, and energy management, and what implications do these interac- tions have for designing user-centric digital energy solutions? The research is structured as follows: Sect. "Back - ground" contextualizes the relevance of app- based energy feedback and user reviews in Nor - way. Sect.
